question.problem: A company manufactures NY Yankees caps at three different plants. Plant $A$ produces $36%$ of the caps, of which $25%$ are white, Plant $B$ produces $34%$ of the caps, of which  $40%$ are white, and Plant $C$ produces the remaining $30%$ of all the caps. If the probability that a randomly selected cap from any of the three plants is white is $0.46,$ what is the probability that a randomly selected cap from plant $C$ is white?
question.worked_solution:
Let $W$ be the event that a randomly selected cap is white, and 

- let $A$ be the event that the cap is from plant $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the cap is from plant $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the cap is from plant $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected cap from any of the three plants is white, we can use the law of total probability:  

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W) & =P(W\cap A)+P(W\cap B)+P(W\cap C) \\  & =P(W|A)P(A)+P(W|B)P(B)+P(W|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since plant $A$ produces $36%$ of all the caps, plant $B$ produces $34%$ of all the caps, and plant $C$ produces $30%$ of all the caps, we have

$$
P(A)=0.36,\,P(B)=0.34,\,P(C)=0.3.
$$

- Since $25%$ of the caps from plant $A$ and $40%$ of the caps from plant $B$ are white, we have

$$
P(W|A)=0.25,\,P(W|B)=0.4.
$$

- Since the probability that a randomly selected cap from any of the three plants is white is $0.46,$ we have 

$$
P(W)=0.46.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(W|C),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W) & =P(W|A)P(A)+P(W|B)P(B)+P(W|C)P(C) \\ 0.46 & =(0.25)(0.36)+(0.4)(0.34)+P(W|C)(0.3) \\ 0.46 & =0.09+0.136+0.3P(W|C) \\ 0.3P(W|C) & =0.234 \\ P(W|C) & =0.78\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected cap from plant $C$ is white is $0.78.$
